title: Character Trailer for an RPG I'm making with AI
author: CinderleafDev

comments.author: Jeduin
comments.body: Hello, that looks interesting, Im very interested to know how you made those animations so fluent.

replies.author: CinderleafDev
replies.body:
Hi, thanks for the comment. Here is some insight:

The poses are ordered by Claude from Codex.

Everything else is done by Claude in the list below after we agreed on methods and learned lessons from previous attempts.

https://i.redd.it/rqz9me5t8txh1.png

replies.author: Jeduin
replies.body: Thats amazing! Been working hard on finding out this sort of information, how to move and animate characters etc.

replies.author: CinderleafDev
replies.body: It's a lot of work, it's not perfect and I still do checks by eye in the end both in game as well as frame by frame. The Art QA list is compacted at this point, but I would say it's about composed of at least 200+ issues I caught in last 2 weeks of nonstop work.

replies.author: Jeduin
replies.body:
poh.. thats insane. but still worth it, the animations are top notch. 

I need to animate around 200 different characters for my game. I'll better start tinkering.

replies.author: CinderleafDev
replies.body: I'd be careful with my method then. A single hero ability you see in the trailer from start to finish takes up to 2 hours between all the checks, then my personal check by eye and testing in the game whether it feels right or not. 2 hours for 1 of 200 characters is a lot of time, and I don't know what each of those characters can do in your game so it might be fine for you, it might be not.
